sections.h2: What written notice must a Michigan landlord give before an eviction case?
sections.html:
Which notice applies turns on the landlord's reason. Unpaid rent brings a 7-day notice. A month-to-month tenancy ends on one month's notice, and a year-to-year tenancy ends one year after service. The legal source for most of these is MCL 554.134, with the court filing rules in MCL 600.5714.

Michigan's court administrators publish fill-in forms for each notice. The Demand for Possession for nonpayment is form DC 100a, the general Notice to Quit is DC 100c, and the drug activity notice is DC 100e. Every form comes in a tenant copy and a court copy; the landlord files away the court copy together with the record of how and when it was delivered.

sections.h2: What proof of service should a Michigan landlord keep?
sections.html:
The court's checklist for both the 7-day demand and the notice to quit has four steps, and a landlord who cannot answer yes to each may have trouble later in court:

  • Fill in the notice form completely, including the tenant's name, the delivery address, the rent owed or the move-out date, and the landlord's own address and phone.
  • Sign it.
  • Deliver the tenant's copy by one of the permitted methods.
  • Keep the court copy, whose certificate of service records the date of delivery, the name of the person who received it and how it was delivered.

That certificate becomes the landlord's evidence when the case reaches the judge, so it should be filled in on the day of delivery and not rebuilt afterward.

sections.h2: How must a Michigan landlord deliver the notice?
sections.html:
The court forms list four valid ways to serve it:

  • Hand it to the tenant in person.
  • Give it on the premises to a family or household member or the tenant's employee, with a request to pass it on.
  • Mail it first class to the last address you have for the tenant. For mail, MCL 600.5718 sets the service date as the next regular delivery day after mailing.
  • Email it, but only if the tenant has consented to electronic service in writing and the consent was confirmed by a reply.

The forms warn about improper service. Slipping the notice under the door, leaving it outside the door, attaching it to the property or mailing it by a method that requires a signature are all examples that can sink the later court case. The 7-day nonpayment form is the minimum, and the lease or another law may require a longer period.

sections.h2: What happens after the Michigan notice period ends?
sections.html:
The landlord can file a complaint in district court. The state court forms for the complaint ask for a copy of the notice or demand. The court then issues a summons.

  • Trial is set within 10 days of the summons being issued, and service must happen 3 or more days ahead of it. Courts with a local rule may instead require appearance 5 days after service.
  • A summary proceeding is heard within 7 days after the tenant appears or the trial date arrives, with adjournments only by stipulation.
  • A case based on the 24-hour drug activity notice is heard on the day the tenant appears and is adjourned only for extraordinary reasons.

If the court finds for the landlord on nonpayment, it fixes the amount due at trial and subtracts any rent excused by the landlord's breach of the lease or statutory covenants. The tenant can stop the writ by paying that amount plus taxed costs within the time provided (MCL 600.5741 and 600.5744(7)).

sections.h2: When can a sheriff or court officer actually remove a Michigan tenant?
sections.html:
Only after the court orders it. MCL 600.5744 directs the court to issue a writ of restitution commanding a court officer, bailiff or sheriff to put the landlord in possession and remove occupants and property. Ordinarily the writ waits for 10 days after judgment.

The court may allow an immediate writ on conditions it sets, for example when the premises have been ordered vacated for lack of a housing certificate, when entry was forcible, when the occupant is a trespasser, when the tenant is causing a serious health hazard or extensive damage, or in a drug activity case. A land contract forfeiture carries a longer wait: 90 days if under half of the price was paid, six months if half or more.

sections.h2: May a landlord change the locks or cut off utilities?
sections.html:
No. MCL 600.2918 treats force, changing locks without handing over keys, boarding up the premises, removing doors or windows, keeping or destroying the tenant's belongings, and cutting off heat, water, electric or gas as unlawful interference. The tenant may claim the larger of real damages or $200 for each incident.

Someone pushed out by force may recover triple actual damages or $200 if that is more, along with possession. A suit to regain possession is due within 90 days of the event or its discovery, and a damages suit within a year. The section cannot be waived in a lease. Exceptions cover court orders, brief entry for repairs or inspection, and good-faith belief that the tenant has abandoned and left rent unpaid.

sections.h2: What does a tenant mean for selling a Michigan house?
sections.html:
A rented house can often be sold occupied, yet a sale does not let the seller bypass the notice rules. The tenancy still ends only through the notice and court steps above, so a buyer who wants vacant possession has to wait out the lease or have the seller serve a proper notice first.

A few sale situations have their own rules. After a mortgage foreclosure sale or an execution sale, a person who stays in the house past the redemption period can be removed by summary proceedings under MCL 600.5714(1)(g). After a probate-licensed sale by a personal representative, the same remedy applies under paragraph (h). Following a foreclosure sale, the purchaser may inspect and, if inspection is unreasonably refused or damage is imminent, may start summary proceedings after giving the mortgagor 7 days' written notice to repair (MCL 600.3238).

Phone the clerk of the district court that covers the rental for local rules and the filing fee.

faqs.q: How many days is a Michigan eviction notice for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Seven days. A landlord may end the tenancy with a written 7-day notice to quit under MCL 554.134(2), and MCL 600.5714(1)(a) opens summary proceedings if the tenant stays past 7 days after a written demand. A lease may call for longer.

faqs.q: Can a Michigan landlord evict someone with a 24-hour notice?
faqs.a: Only for controlled substance activity when the lease has a termination clause and a formal police report has been filed. Under MCL 554.134(4) the notice is 24 hours. Other violations use longer notice periods.

faqs.q: Does a Michigan landlord need a court order to remove a tenant?
faqs.a: Yes. Yes. Once the notice runs out, the landlord files in district court, obtains a judgment and then waits for a writ of restitution, ordinarily 10 days later. Court officers or the sheriff carry it out.

faqs.q: What if a Michigan landlord changes the locks without a court order?
faqs.a: The tenant may recover actual damages or $200, whichever is greater, per occurrence under MCL 600.2918, and may recover possession. A tenant should file within 90 days to regain possession.

faqs.q: How much notice does a monthly tenant get?
faqs.a: One month. If rent is payable at intervals shorter than 3 months, the notice period equals the payment interval. A year-to-year tenancy ends 1 year after service of the notice.
